chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from whom he mentioned from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, is the Fitrah (Zakat al-Fitr) obligatory upon the people of the countryside?' He said, then he said, 'The Fitrah is obligatory upon every person who consumes sustenance, so upon him is to pay from that sustance.'

key_terms.الْفِطْرَةُ: Zakat al-Fitr, the alms-giving given at the end of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: Who is obligated to pay Zakat al-Fitr according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify that the obligation of Fitrah is tied to the consumption of basic sustenance rather than geographic location, thereby extending the duty to rural populations (Ahl al-Bawadi) equally with urban dwellers. This ruling underscores the universality of the obligation in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that the criterion is economic capacity to afford food rather than residence, ensuring the poor are supported regardless of their community's structure.
